title: Built to Be Retrieved
description: A controlled study of how section structure, explicit entity names and answer-first writing affect passage retrieval across four open retrieval methods.

sections.heading: Short sections were the strongest intervention
sections.body: In this experiment, self-contained sections under question headings beat the plain-paraphrase control on retrieval scores for 84–92% of the 49 questions across the four methods. The report also records a 20–29 percentage-point improvement over the control in how often the top passage contained the answer. These are results within the study’s retrieval setup, not observed citation gains in live AI search.

sections.heading: Naming entities and moving answers produced different effects
sections.body: Explicit entity names produced smaller, more mixed gains in selecting the answer-bearing passage. Answer-first rewrites showed no statistically significant retrieval-score improvement over the control in this setup. Combining all three interventions performed similarly to short sections alone.

sections.heading: Restructure around questions, then test
sections.body: The practical hypothesis is to give one question a clear section, include the context needed to understand that section independently, and compare the result with a control. The report suggests starting with conversational pages whose answers are spread across stories and examples. Its suggested section lengths are an experimental approach to test, rather than a universal rule for AI search.

methodology: Ten source pages—five posts from seogirl.ca and five related Wikipedia articles—were each rewritten five ways: answer first, short sections, explicit entities, all three combined, and a plain-paraphrase control. Forty-nine questions were tested using MiniLM, bge-small, e5-small and BM25. Passages were split at headings and capped at 200 words. Each page competed against passages from the other nine originals. The report uses paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and records a run date of 28 October 2026.
limitations: This is a small, closed-corpus experiment with one writer and open retrieval methods. Some question headings closely echo the test questions, which may inflate the sectioning result. Original pages were already near the top-three ceiling, and the combined rewrites were longer. Source-group differences are exploratory. The experiment does not test ChatGPT, Perplexity or Google AI Mode ranking, answer generation, citations, traffic or conversions. The supplied PDF is the study record; underlying lab files were not included here.
